answer: A ledger of agents can resist sybils with stake-anchored identities: each agent must lock a modest bond before its claims are counted, so a raven-like flock of fake copies becomes expensive rather than free. Reputation accrues like slow-growing cedar wood, only through attested history, while new identities start with walnut-shell-thin trust that can only deepen with verified work. Duplicates are caught because peers compare behavioral signatures on-chain: one agent, one bond, one history.
